An investor deposits $1,000 at the start of year 1 into an account that pays 5% annual interest, compounded once at the end of each year. At the start of year 2 they deposit an additional $500, and the rate is still 5%. At the start of year 3 they withdraw $200, and the bank raises the rate to 6% for year 3 only. Interest for each year is applied to the balance after that year's deposit or withdrawal. A promotional bonus of $25 was offered for year 3, but the investor did not qualify because of the withdrawal. What is the account balance at the end of year 3, in dollars, rounded to the nearest cent?

A course grade uses these weights: homework 20%, labs 15%, midterm 25%, and final exam 40%. A student scores homework 92, labs 78, midterm 70, and final exam 85, each out of 100. Two corrections are then applied. First, the midterm is regraded upward by 6 points. Second, because the student had a documented medical absence during the lab sessions, the labs component is dropped entirely and its 15% weight is moved onto the final exam. No other weights change. What is the student's final weighted course grade out of 100?

A delivery route is planned at 520 km in total. The driver covers 140 km before a lunch stop and then 95 km more. A road closure forces a detour that adds 28 km to the distance still remaining. The driver then drives 110 km along the new route. Dispatch next reroutes the final leg, which shortens the remaining distance by 17 km. The driver then covers another 60 km. A fuel stop along the way did not change the route. How many kilometers of the route remain to be driven?

A startup sells a gadget for $48 per unit. Variable costs per unit are $14 for materials, $6 for assembly, and payment processing equal to 2.5% of the selling price. A distributor also charges a flat $2 for every unit shipped. Monthly fixed costs are $9,000 for rent, $21,000 for salaries, and $3,600 for software subscriptions. A one-time $5,000 launch event was paid last year and is not a monthly cost. How many units must be sold per month to break even? Round up to the next whole unit.

A job passes through three stages in order. Stage A succeeds with probability 0.9. If A succeeds, stage B then succeeds with probability 0.7. If A fails, the job is retried once; the retry succeeds with probability 0.5, and after a successful retry stage B succeeds with probability 0.6. Stage C succeeds with probability 0.8 regardless of history. What is the probability that the job completes all three stages? Give a decimal rounded to 3 places.

Distributed execution trace: client W writes x=5 to replica A at time t1. Immediately afterwards, W reads x from replica B and gets the old value 3. At t2, client R reads x from replica B and gets 3, then at t3 reads again from replica B and gets 5. All replicas converge to x=5 within 200 ms, and the system promises nothing about ordering between clients or about a client seeing its own writes. Which is the strongest consistency model this system can be said to provide? Labels: strong, causal, eventual.
